simple.meaning: סַפִּיר (çappîyr) is a Hebrew word meaning “a gem (perhaps used for scratching other substances), probably the sapphire.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: סַפִּיר (H5601) appears 11 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 24:10, with occurrences in Exodus, Job, Song of Solomon, Isaiah, Lamentations, and 1 more.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to סַפִּיר (H5601) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in סַפִּיר (H5601) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: סַפִּיר (çappîyr) / H5601 is traced through Exodus 24:10, Exodus 28:18, Exodus 39:11, Job 28:6 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.short: a gem (perhaps used for scratching other substances), probably the sapphire
definitions.full: H5601. sappir סַמִּיר noun [masculine] sapphire , perhaps also lapis lazuli (compare Di Exod 24:10 Now Archaeology i. 131 ) (Late Hebrew id. , and סַמְמִּירִינוֺן ; סַמִּרִינוֺן ᵑ7 ; ᵑ6 ; loan-word from Sanskrit canipriya according to Lag Ges. Abh. 72 Lewy Fremdw. 56 compare Greek σάπφειρος ); — absolute ׳ס 24:10 8 t.; plural סַמִּירִים Isa 54:11 ; Song 5:14 ; — with other jewels as ornaments of prince Ezek 28:13 ; in high priest's breastplate Exod 28:18 ; 39:11 ; found in mines Job 28:6 , costly 28:16 compare Isa 54:11 ; taking high polish Lam 4:7 (in figurative); סַמִּירִים מְעֻלֶּפֶת שֵׁן Song 5:14 ivory covered with sapphires (in figurative); lapis lazuli , according to Hi BU Du and others in Job 28:6 ( לוֺ זָהָב עַפְרֹת being understood of sparkling crystals of iron pyrites in this), but see Di; lapis lazuli may be intended in הַסּ ׳לִבְנַת Exod 24:10 (J) pavement of sapphire (in theoph.), compare ׳אֶבֶןסֿ Ezek 1:26 ; 10:1 .
